messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning a telemetry-agent rollout during the maintenance window in az25. Agent v2.4 causes a short CPU spike in kubelet sidecars during startup which can push some GPU pods into OOM-ish conditions. We need to drain nodes to be safe. Target window: Tue 2026-04-07 00:00-03:00 UTC. Plan: rolling drains, 3–5 nodes at a time, validate KV-cache and model latency, then continue. Will reserve extra capacity before starting.

sam: Can we do smaller batches (2–3 nodes)? 5 at a time might starve embeddings and long-running tuning jobs. What's current spare capacity in az25?

maya: Current spare ~= 8 nodes (burst pool). I propose pre-reserving 10 nodes from the burst pool and pre-warming them with KV-cache seed. That keeps effective spare >15% during the window. I'll trigger reservations 30m before start.

jordan: Quick cost note: reserving 10 nodes for ~3h is nontrivial — estimate ballpark $1.2k depending on instance type. If we pre-warm, that will add network/IO but reduces SLA risk. Recommend tagging spend `maintenance:telemetry-rollout`.

lee: Network note — the agent emits a telemetry burst (~2–3MB/s per node) for the first 90s. Could spike egress. Suggest we set an initial rate-limit flag to 200KB/s and allow it to ramp over 5m. Also double-check netpols so telemetry egress isn't blocked during rollout.

maya: Agreed on rate-limit. Runbook snippet (for each node):

```
# cordon + drain + label
kubectl cordon node/$NODE
kubectl drain node/$NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=critical' --timeout=15m
kubectl label node/$NODE telemetry-upgrade=rolling-2026-04-07
```

After drain, smoke: `curl -sS http://node.$NODE.health/metrics | grep telemetry_startup` -> expect 'ok'. If not, re-schedule node back and escalate.

tess: I'll draft a short external note for Support: "Planned maintenance in az25 — transient queueing for some jobs, no data loss expected. Window 00:00–03:00 UTC Tue 2026-04-07. We will reroute traffic if latency degrades." I'll post to #support 24h before.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: MNT-9876. Notifying on-call and auto-creating incident channel. :robot_face:

sam: One more idea — can we add a temporary routing rule to shift up to 20% of model inference traffic to eu-central if ready_replicas in az25 dips below 80%? That will cost inter-region egress but protects p99 latency.

maya: Yes. We'll add fallback routing: if availability < 80% for more than 30s, shift 20% traffic to eu-central for up to 10m and then re-evaluate. Adding to runbook.

jordan: Approve the cost tradeoff for SLA protection. Also please ensure finance tags are applied so we can reconcile the maintenance spend.

lee: Testing plan: simulate 4 concurrent drains in staging with KV-cache load and real inference traffic; measure token latency and egress. I'll run the test and share results by EOD today.

maya: Thanks — plan locked. Reservation will be requested at 23:30 UTC day-of. First drain begins 00:05 UTC. I'll post the final comms 24h prior and a short follow-up after completion. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

tess: :wave: drafting comm now, will ping once posted.
